duration_ms.description: Wall-clock duration of this node's execution.

error.description: Failure reason. Present iff `status = "failed"` (or `"skipped"` due to upstream failure).

label.description: Human-readable label (usually the pipeline or model name).

layer.description: Layer index (0-based): the node's ordering position in the DAG. Same-layer nodes are dispatched together, but nodes that share a state file execute one at a time — so a shared layer bounds ordering, not wall-clock overlap. Seed nodes and nodes writing distinct state files do run concurrently.

Diagnostic.description:
A compiler diagnostic (error, warning, or informational message).

`code` and `message` use `Arc<str>` (§P3.5) — cloning a `Diagnostic` in the LSP publish loop becomes a refcount bump. Construction still accepts any `Into<String>` / `&str` via the helper constructors below; the arc wrap happens once at construction time.

model.description: Which model this diagnostic relates to.

Severity.description:
Severity level of a diagnostic.

Serialized in PascalCase (`"Error"`, `"Warning"`, `"Info"`) to stay compatible with existing dagster fixtures and the hand-written `Severity` StrEnum in `integrations/dagster/src/dagster_rocky/types.py`.

description: Output of `rocky run --dag`: per-node execution results plus aggregate counts.

consumer_diagnostics.description: Problems in the project's `consumers/` records (`E060`). Reported once for the whole graph; they never fail a node. Empty (and omitted) when the records are sound.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock duration of the entire DAG execution.

failed.description: Nodes whose dispatcher returned an error.

nodes.description: Per-node execution records, sorted by (layer, id).

skipped.description: Nodes skipped because an upstream failed (or because the dispatcher declined to handle them, e.g. Test nodes).

total_layers.description: Number of execution layers (Kahn topological depth).

warnings.description: Scheduling warnings from dependency inference — physical-read derivation (mutual reads serialized deterministically, unparseable models, colliding targets) and label inference (label collisions where only one claimant orders the reader, unparseable models). Empty when none.
